# Plugins

Add published packages, versioned packages, scoped packages, or local plugin directories to `opencode.json(c)`.

## Configure

```jsonc title="opencode.jsonc"
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": [
    "opencode-acme-plugin",
    "opencode-acme-plugin@1.2.0",
    "@acme/opencode-plugin",
    "./plugins/local",
    "../shared/plugin",
    "/absolute/path/plugin",
    "file:///home/me/plugins/local",
    {
      "package": "@acme/opencode-plugin",
      "options": {
        "agent": "reviewer",
        "strict": true,
      },
    },
  ],
}
```

Relative paths resolve from the config file containing the entry.

Configured local paths must be directories. A path to a single file is skipped. See [Load](/build/plugins#load) for
how OpenCode finds each part in a directory.

Plugin arrays from applicable config files are applied from lowest to highest precedence instead of replacing one
another.

```text
~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc
./opencode.jsonc
./.opencode/opencode.jsonc
```

## Discover

OpenCode also loads direct `.ts` and `.js` files and immediate plugin package directories from every discovered
`.opencode/plugins/` directory.

```text
.opencode/
└── plugins/
    ├── concise.ts
    ├── reviewer.js
    └── acme-package/
```

Global plugins use the same discovery layout under the OpenCode config directory.

```text
~/.config/opencode/plugins/
```

A `plugins/` directory beside a project-root `opencode.json(c)` is not discovered automatically; configure its plugin
directories explicitly or move it under `.opencode/`.

```jsonc title="opencode.jsonc"
{
  "plugins": ["./plugins/local"]
}
```

## Control

Plugin entries are processed in order. Prefix an ID or wildcard with `-` to disable it, use `*` for every plugin, and
use `.*` to match an ID prefix. A later ID re-enables a plugin.

```jsonc title="opencode.jsonc"
{
  "plugins": ["*", "-opencode.provider.*", "opencode.provider.openai", "-acme.reviewer"]
}
```

To disable the notice added to new forks, add `"-opencode.fork-notice"` to `plugins`.

Two built-in plugins ignore removals so that a repository cannot switch off
[policy](/policies) enforcement: `opencode.config.policy` and
`opencode.provider.opencode`, the Console connection that delivers organization
policy.

## Manage

Install, list, check, update, or remove global package plugins with the CLI.

```sh
opencode plugin add opencode-acme-plugin@1.2.0
opencode plugin list
opencode plugin list --builtin
opencode plugin check
opencode plugin update
opencode plugin update opencode-acme-plugin
opencode plugin remove opencode-acme-plugin@1.2.0
```

`plugin check` checks server, GUI-only, and TUI-only package plugins for updates. `plugin update` updates every outdated package;
pass a configured package target to check or update only that package. Local plugins and exact package revisions are
skipped.

Package installation accepts npm names with versions, tags, or ranges, plus npm-compatible Git package specifications.
Git repositories can use hosted shortcuts, HTTPS, or SSH, including private repositories available through your existing
Git credentials.

```sh
opencode plugin add @acme/opencode-plugin@latest
opencode plugin add github:acme/opencode-plugin
opencode plugin add git+ssh://git@github.com/acme/opencode-plugin.git#main
opencode plugin add 'github:acme/plugins#main::path:packages/opencode-plugin'
```

Branches, tags, complete commit hashes, and npm's `::path:` repository-subdirectory selectors are supported. Configure
local paths directly; tarball and npm alias targets are not accepted by `plugin add`.

## Reload

Changes under watched config directories reload automatically. Server startup loads cached package plugins immediately,
installs missing packages in the background, and checks unpinned npm and Git plugins for updates without changing the
installed package. Exact npm versions and full Git commit hashes stay pinned. Changes to unwatched local dependencies
may still require restarting OpenCode.

```sh
touch .opencode/plugins/concise/index.ts
opencode service restart
```

## Desktop

A plugin that exports `./gui-experimental` also adds panels, commands, or settings to OpenCode Desktop. The app loads
plugins from the server it runs, so configure the plugin in your global `opencode.json(c)` to use it in every window.

```jsonc title="~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc"
{
  "plugins": ["opencode-acme-plugin"],
}
```

**Settings > Extensions > Plugins** lists them when the app's own server is selected. A plugin's switch turns off only
its desktop UI, and **Reload** loads it again after a failure. To turn off the whole plugin, add `-` and its ID to
`plugins`, for example `"-acme"`.

## Terminal

TUI-only plugins are configured separately and remain active when connected to a remote server.

```json title="cli.json"
{
  "plugins": ["opencode-acme-cli"]
}
```

## Objective
Demonstrate the autonomous Codeguardian pipeline: manual trigger → verify.sh → Reviewer → Vault note with log evidence.

## Requirements
- Communication in German, address as "Boss".
- Reviewer model: `ollama/codellama:latest`.
- Builder: OmniRoute (`freellmapi/auto`).
- Evidence: Log entries + Sub-Agent session IDs in Vault notes.

## Decisions
- Manual triggering via CLI script instead of event-based due to lack of `session.idle` support in OpenCode.

## Work State
### Completed
- Diagnosed and confirmed lack of `orchestrator.log` and `session.idle` events.
- Created `run-review.js` as entry point for manual triggering.
- Refactored `orchestrator.js` to provide central pipeline logic via `run()` function.

### Active
- Testing manual execution via `node .opencode/plugins/run-review.js`.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Verify log evidence and document Sub-Agent session IDs.
2. Ensure Vault note is created with proper log evidence.

## Relevant Files
- `.opencode/plugins/auto-review.js`: Reference architecture for pipeline logic.
- `.opencode/plugins/orchestrator.js`: Central pipeline control.
- `.opencode/plugins/run-review.js`: Entry point for manual triggering.
- `scripts/verify.sh`: 143 Doctest tests, EXIT=0 (current status).
- `codeguardian/`: Target directory for review notes.

## Important Context
- OpenCode Plugin API does not support `session.idle` events.
- `auto-review.js` uses proven pattern: `git status --porcelain` checks for changes, then runs `bash scripts/verify.sh`, followed by `client.session.prompt({ model, agent: "reviewer" })`.
- No hardcoded secrets; all provider environment variables via ENV (`REVIEWER_MODEL`, `OMNIROUTE_API_KEY`).

## Requirements
- Kommunikation auf Deutsch, Anrede "Boss".

- Builder: OmniRoute (`freellmapi/auto`).
- Evidenz: Log-Einträge + Sub-Agent-Session-IDs in Vault-Notes.
- Manuelle Auslösung via CLI-Skript (keine `session.idle`-Events in OpenCode verfügbar).

## Decisions
- Manuelle Pipeline via `run-review.js` statt Event-basiertem Plugin.
- Git Bash verwenden (`C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe`) statt WSL bash (nicht vorhanden).

### Completed
- `orchestrator.log` und `session.idle`-Event-Support als nicht verfügbar diagnostiziert.

- Git Bash als verfügbare Shell-Option identifiziert.

### Active
- Fix für `run-review.js`: Pfad zu Git Bash explizit setzen, damit `verify.sh` auf Windows läuft.

### Blocked
- WSL bash fehlt (`CreateProcessCommon:818: execvpe(/bin/bash) failed: No such file or directory`).

## Next Move
1. `run-review.js` aktualisieren: `bash` durch `"C:/Program Files/Git/bin/bash.exe"` ersetzen.
2. Pipeline erneut testen: `node .opencode/plugins/run-review.js`.
3. verify.sh-Ausgabe und Exit-Code dokumentieren.

## Relevant Files
- `.opencode/plugins/run-review.js`: Entry-Point, benötigt Git Bash-Pfad-Fix.
- `scripts/verify.sh`: 143 Doctest-Tests, wird von Pipeline ausgeführt.
- `.opencode/plugins/auto-review.js`: Referenz-Architektur für Pipeline-Logik.

- `auto-review.js` nutzt bewährtes Pattern: `git status --porcelain` prüft Änderungen, dann `bash scripts/verify.sh`, dann `client.session.prompt()` mit Reviewer-Modell.
- Keine Hardcoded Secrets; Provider-ENV-Vars über `.env` (`REVIEWER_MODEL`, `OMNIROUTE_API_KEY`).

- `REVIEWER_MODEL` aus `.env` per `grep` gelesen (Default `ollama/codellama:latest`).
- Note-Name und `dateien` aus `git status --porcelain` abgeleitet.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Codeguardian-Pipeline: pytest Doctest-Runner
# Aufruf: bash scripts/verify.sh [Pfad]
# Exit 0 = bestanden, Exit != 0 = fehlgeschlagen

TARGET="${1:-.}"

echo "=== Codeguardian verify.sh ==="
echo "Ziel: $TARGET"
echo ""

# Wenn TARGET="." (ganzes Repo), prüfe nur geänderte .py-Dateien via git
# Das vermeidet ffmpeg-Trigger in unbenutzten Modulen und beschleunigt die Prüfung
if [[ "$TARGET" == "." ]]; then
  # Git-Repo? Falls ja, nur geänderte Dateien prüfen
  if git rev-parse --git-dir > /dev/null 2>&1; then
    # Staged + unstaged + untracked .py-Dateien sammeln
    mapfile -t FILES < <(git status --porcelain | awk '{print $2}' | grep '\.py$' || true)
    if [[ ${#FILES[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
      echo "Prüfe ${#FILES[@]} geänderte .py-Dateien:"
      for f in "${FILES[@]}"; do
        echo "  - $f"
      done
      echo ""
      # pytest nur auf diesen Dateien
      python -m pytest \
        --doctest-modules \
        -v \
        --tb=short \
        --capture=no \
        "${FILES[@]}"
      exit $?
    else
      echo "Keine .py-Änderungen erkannt — übersprungen"
      exit 0
    fi
  fi
fi

## Objective
- Codeguardian-Pipeline über manuelles Trigger-Skript `run-review.js` end-to-end lauffähig machen: `verify.sh` → Reviewer-Agent via Ollama → Vault-Note mit Evidenz.

## Requirements
- Pipeline manuell über `run-review.js` auslösbar.
- Git-Bash-Pfad auf Windows: `C:/Program Files/Git/bin/bash.exe` (in pwsh wegen Leerzeichen in Anführungszeichen setzen).
- Evidenz in Vault-Note: `verify.sh`-stdout, Exit-Code, Reviewer-Antwort/Session-ID.
- Format: YAML-Frontmatter + Sections Ergebnis/Schritt-Abgleich/Input-Output/verify.sh.
- Reviewer-Modell konfigurierbar über `.env`-Variable `REVIEWER_MODEL` (Default: `ollama/codellama:latest`).

## Decisions
- Manueller Einstieg über `run-review.js` statt `session.idle`.
- Reviewer-Call direkt über Ollama HTTP-API (`fetch("http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/generate")`), da freistehendes Node-Skript kein OpenCode-SDK hat.
- Note-Name und `dateien` aus `git status --porcelain` abgeleitet, auf `\.py$` gefiltert.
- `REVIEWER_MODEL` nativ per `fs.readFileSync(DOTENV)` + Regex gelesen.
- verify.sh-Aufruf mit Argument `.` (`bash.exe scripts/verify.sh .`).
- `verify.sh` um Git-geänderte-Dateien-Modus erweitert: bei `TARGET=.` nur geänderte `.py`-Dateien via `git status --porcelain` sammeln, pytest nur darauf; Fallback mit `--ignore`-Liste für explizite Pfade.
- Filter in `verify.sh` muss noch verengt werden (Stray-/Scratch-Dateien mit Side-Effects ausschließen) — Entscheidung offen.

### Completed
- `run-review.js` komplett geschrieben und per Read bestätigt (186 Zeilen): natives .env-Parsing, Ollama-HTTP-Call (120 s Timeout), verify.sh via Git Bash, Note-Write nach `codeguardian/`, CLI-Entry-Point, Log nach `.opencode/run-review.log`.

- `verify.sh` editiert und vollständig re-gelesen (91 Zeilen): Git-geänderte-Dateien-Modus in Zeilen 17–29 bestätigt, Fallback intakt.
- Bestätigt: `python -m pytest --doctest-modules projects/csv2json/src/csv2json.py` läuft sauber (4 Doctests); pytest 9.1.1.
- Ollama erreichbar: `http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/tags`, Modell `codellama:latest` vorhanden.
- Volle `git status --porcelain`-Liste erhalten: einzige getrackten Änderungen sind ` M 00-Home/Index.md`, ` M OMNI-INBOX.md`, ` M opencode.json`, ` M scripts/verify.sh`; alles andere ist `??` untracked (u. a. `check_api.py`, `02_ECC/`, `code/`, `codeguardian/`-Notes, `__pycache__/`).

## Objective
- Codeguardian-Pipeline über manuelles Trigger-Skript `run-review.js` end-to-end lauffähig machen: `verify.sh` → Reviewer-Agent via Ollama → Vault-Note mit Evidenz.

## Requirements
- Pipeline manuell über `run-review.js` auslösbar.
- Git-Bash-Pfad auf Windows: `C:/Program Files/Git/bin/bash.exe` (in pwsh wegen Leerzeichen in Anführungszeichen setzen).
- Evidenz in Vault-Note: `verify.sh`-stdout, Exit-Code, Reviewer-Antwort/Session-ID.
- Format: YAML-Frontmatter + Sections Ergebnis/Schritt-Abgleich/Input-Output/verify.sh.
- Reviewer-Modell konfigurierbar über `.env`-Variable `REVIEWER_MODEL` (Default: `ollama/codellama:latest`).

## Decisions
- Manueller Einstieg über `run-review.js` statt `session.idle`.
- Reviewer-Call direkt über Ollama HTTP-API (`fetch("http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/generate")`), da freistehendes Node-Skript kein OpenCode-SDK hat.
- Note-Name und `dateien` aus `git status --porcelain` abgeleitet, auf `\.py$` gefiltert.
- `REVIEWER_MODEL` nativ per `fs.readFileSync(DOTENV)` + Regex gelesen.
- verify.sh-Aufruf mit Argument `.` (`bash.exe scripts/verify.sh .`); Log jetzt in `verify-run.log` im Workspace-Root.
- `verify.sh` um Git-geänderte-Dateien-Modus erweitert (TARGET=`.` → `git status --porcelain`); Fallback mit `--ignore`-Liste für explizite Pfade intakt.
- Code-Mode-`execute`-Tool kann kein `require`/Node-Builtins → shell-Befehle über `shell`-Tool ausführen.
- Exit-Code-Check in pwsh: `echo "EXIT=$?"` liefert nur boolesch (`True`/`False`); echter Exit-Code nur via `$LASTEXITCODE`.

- `run-review.js` komplett geschrieben und per Read bestätigt (186 Zeilen): natives .env-Parsing, Ollama-HTTP-Call (120 s Timeout), verify.sh via Git Bash, Note-Write nach `codeguardian/`, CLI-Entry-Point, Log nach `.opencode/run-review.log`.

- Codeguardian-Pipeline über manuelles Trigger-Skript `run-review.js` end-to-end lauffähig machen: `verify.sh` → Reviewer-Agent via Ollama → Vault-Note mit Evidenz.

## Requirements
- Pipeline manuell über `run-review.js` auslösbar.
- Git-Bash-Pfad auf Windows: `C:/Program Files/Git/bin/bash.exe` (in pwsh wegen Leerzeichen in Anführungszeichen setzen).
- Evidenz in Vault-Note: `verify.sh`-stdout, Exit-Code, Reviewer-Antwort/Session-ID.
- Format: YAML-Frontmatter + Sections Ergebnis/Schritt-Abgleich/Input-Output/verify.sh.
- Reviewer-Modell konfigurierbar über `.env`-Variable `REVIEWER_MODEL` (Default: `ollama/codellama:latest`).

## Decisions
- Manueller Einstieg über `run-review.js` statt `session.idle`.
- Reviewer-Call direkt über Ollama HTTP-API (`fetch("http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/generate")`), da freistehendes Node-Skript kein OpenCode-SDK hat.
- Note-Name und `dateien` aus `git status --porcelain` abgeleitet, auf `\.py$` gefiltert.
- `REVIEWER_MODEL` nativ per `fs.readFileSync(DOTENV)` + Regex gelesen.
- verify.sh-Aufruf mit Argument `.` (`bash.exe scripts/verify.sh .`); Log in `verify-run.log` im Workspace-Root.
- `verify.sh` mit Git-geänderte-Dateien-Modus (TARGET=`.` → `git status --porcelain`); Fallback mit `--ignore`-Liste für explizite Pfade intakt.
- Stray-Scratch-Dateien-Problem über `.gitignore` gelöst (nicht Filter in verify.sh): `check_api.py`, `inspect_db*.py`, `mini_beispiel.py`, `remove_duplicates.py`, `run_check.py`, `tmp_inspect_db.py` ignoriert → verschwinden aus `git status`, Git-Modus bleibt generisch.
- Code-Mode-`execute`-Tool kann kein `require`/Node-Builtins → shell-Befehle über `shell`-Tool ausführen.
- Exit-Code-Check in pwsh: `echo "EXIT=$?"` liefert nur boolesch; echter Exit-Code via `$LASTEXITCODE` (setzt sich auch bei `| Out-String` korrekt).
- Offene Strategie: pytest-Exit-5 ("no tests ran") in verify.sh als bestanden behandeln, wenn geänderte .py-Dateien keine Doctests enthalten (noch nicht umgesetzt).
- Ollama-Timeout in run-review.js (aktuell 120 s) reicht für `codellama:latest` mit vollem Review-Prompt nicht — Timeout-Anhebung und/oder Prompt-Reduktion zu entscheiden.

## Work State
Break the objective into smaller goals and report which are completed, which are being worked on, and which are blocked.
### Completed
- `run-review.js` komplett geschrieben und per Read bestätigt (186 Zeilen): natives .env-Parsing, Ollama-HTTP-Call (120 s Timeout), verify.sh via Git Bash, Note-Write nach `codeguardian/`, CLI-Entry-Point, Log nach `.opencode/run-review.log`.
- Entry-Check-Fix angewendet (basename-Vergleich).
- `verify.sh` mit Git-geänderte-Dateien-Modus editiert (Zeilen 17–29), Fallback intakt; vollständiger Re-Read bestätigt.
- `python -m pytest --doctest-modules projects/csv2json/src/csv2json.py` läuft sauber (4 Doctests); pytest 9.1.1.
- Ollama erreichbar: `http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/tags`, Modell `codellama:latest` vorhanden.
- `.gitignore`-Edit angewendet (6 Root-Scratch-Dateien ignoriert) → Stray-Dateien-Problem gelöst.
- Revalidierung `verify.sh .`: nur noch 2 geänderte .py-Dateien (`scripts/__init__.py`, `scripts/check_providers.py`), kein DB-Dump, saubere kurze Ausgabe.
- Commit-Status von `projects/csv2json/src/csv2json.py` geprüft: im Commit `14aa7e32` enthalten, Working Tree sauber.
- Erster End-to-End-Lauf `node .opencode/plugins/run-review.js` (via Git Bash): Diff-Erkennung (2 Dateien), verify.sh-Lauf (exit=5, ok=false), Note nach `codeguardian/` geschrieben — aber Ollama-Call timeouted (120 s), Note enthält nur `## Fehler: The operation was aborted due to timeout`.

### Active
- **Ollama-Timeout-Fix**: run-review.js-Timeout anheben (z. B. 300 s) und/oder Review-Prompt kürzen; danach Re-Lauf, damit die Vault-Note eine echte Reviewer-Antwort statt Fehler-Sektion enthält.
- **verify.sh liefert Exit 5** (pytest "no tests ran"): geänderte `scripts/__init__.py`/`scripts/check_providers.py` haben keine Doctests → 0 collected → Exit 5. Pipeline liest das als Fehlschlag; Fix fehlt (Exit 5 → als bestanden/übersprungen behandeln oder nur doctest-tragende Dateien prüfen), danach Revalidierung mit `$LASTEXITCODE` (Erwartung 0).
- OMNI-INBOX.md-Eintrag auf `- [x]` setzen + Lösung notieren.
- Artefakt-Datei `C：UsersDirkBielerAppDataLocalTempopencodeverify_run5.log` löschen; `verify-run.log` aufräumen.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. `run-review.js`: Ollama-Timeout von 120 s erhöhen (mind. 300 s) und ggf. Review-Prompt kürzen; Re-Lauf `node .opencode/plugins/run-review.js` → Vault-Note soll echte Reviewer-Antwort + Session-ID enthalten.
2. `scripts/verify.sh`: pytest-Exit-5 behandeln (nach `python -m pytest ...` Exit-Code prüfen; bei 5 → "Keine auswertbaren Doctests in geänderten Dateien" + `exit 0`), Revalidierung `& "C:/Program Files/Git/bin/bash.exe" scripts/verify.sh .` + `$LASTEXITCODE` (Erwartung: 0).
3. Für echten csv2json-Review-Pfad (Datei ist committed, steht nicht mehr in git status): expliziten Lauf `bash.exe scripts/verify.sh projects/csv2json/src/csv2json.py` oder run-review.js mit Target.
4. Artefakt-Datei `C：UsersDirkBielerAppDataLocalTempopencodeverify_run5.log` + `verify-run.log` aufräumen.
5. OMNI-INBOX.md: Eintrag auf `- [x]` setzen, Lösung notieren.

## Relevant Files
- `E:\AI-System 3.0\.opencode\plugins\run-review.js`: Trigger-Skript (.env-Parsing, Ollama-Call mit 120 s Timeout, Note-Write, Logging) — Timeout-Fix als nächstes hier.
- `E:\AI-System 3.0\scripts\verify.sh`: pytest Doctest-Runner; Git-Modus (Zeilen 17–29); braucht Exit-5-Handling (derzeit `exit $?` propagiert pytest-Exit-5 ungeprüft).
- `E:\AI-System 3.0\codeguardian\PRUEFUNG-2026-11-11T15-18-45.md`: Note des ersten E2E-Laufs — enthält nur Ollama-Timeout-Fehler, keine Review; als Evidenz/Format-Beispiel.
- `E:\AI-System 3.0\codeguardian\PRUEFUNG-csv2json-2026-11-11T12-30-00.md`: Format-Vorbild für Vault-Notes.
- `E:\AI-System 3.0\projects\csv2json\src\csv2json.py`: Ziel-Modul mit 4 Doctests; committed (`14aa7e32`), nicht mehr in `git status` → nur über expliziten Pfad prüfbar.
- `E:\AI-System 3.0\scripts\__init__.py`, `E:\AI-System 3.0\scripts\check_providers.py`: einzige geänderte .py-Dateien nach Gitignore-Fix; ohne Doctests (Ursache Exit 5).
- `E:\AI-System 3.0\.gitignore`: editiert — 6 Root-Scratch-Dateien ignoriert.
- `E:\AI-System 3.0\.opencode\run-review.log`: Log des E2E-Durchlaufs von run-review.js.
- `E:\AI-System 3.0\verify-run.log`: Volle Ausgabe des alten `verify.sh .`-Laufs — Aufräum-Kandidat.
- `E:\AI-System 3.0\.env`: `REVIEWER_MODEL=ollama/codellama:latest`.
- `E:\AI-System 3.0\OMNI-INBOX.md`: Inbox-Eintrag (in-progress), zum Abschluss.
- `E:\AI-System 3.0\C：UsersDirkBielerAppDataLocalTempopencodeverify_run5.log`: Artefakt-Müll, kann gelöscht werden.

## Important Context
- Ollama-Call in run-review.js hat beim E2E-Lauf nach 120 s getimed out (`The operation was aborted due to timeout`) — `codellama:latest` war im Benchmark ~36 s für kurze Prompts, der volle Review-Prompt dauert länger; Timeout-Fix steht aus.
- Node-Warnung beim E2E-Lauf: `MODULE_TYPELESS_PACKAGE_JSON` — run-review.js wird als ES Module geparst; optional `"type": "module"` in `.opencode/package.json` ergänzen.
- pytest-Exit-Codes: 5 = "no tests ran" — verify.sh Zeile 27 `exit $?` propagiert ihn; Pipeline (Exit ≠ 0 → "fehlgeschlagen") würde ihn falsch bewerten.
- Nach Gitignore-Fix zeigt `git status` nur noch: ` M 00-Home/Index.md`, ` M OMNI-INBOX.md`, ` M opencode.json`, ` M scripts/verify.sh`, ` M .gitignore`, plus untracked: `scripts/__init__.py`, `scripts/check_providers.py`, `projects/code-guardian-engine/`, `projects/json2csv/`, `projects/tiktok-analysis/`, `projects/csv2json/src/__pycache__/`.
- Session-Shell ist pwsh: `C:/Program Files/Git/bin/bash.exe` als Ganzes in Anführungszeichen; Unix-Pipes nur via `bash.exe -c "..."`; echter Exit-Code via `$LASTEXITCODE` (auch hinter `| Out-String`), nicht `echo "EXIT=$?"` (Boolean True/False).
- Code-Mode-`execute`-Runtime hat kein `require`/`fs`/`child_process` — für Shell-Aufrufe `shell`-Tool verwenden.
- Vollrepo-pytest (`.`) blockiert beim Collect an ffmpeg/av-C-Plugin-Importen (`code/video-analyse/`, `02_ECC/tests/`) — Git-Modus vermeidet das.
- Python: `C:\Users\DirkBieler\AppData\Local\Programs\Python\Python312\python.exe`, pytest 9.1.1.

## Objective
- Make the Codeguardian-Pipeline work end-to-end via manual trigger script `run-review.js`: `verify.sh` → Reviewer-Agent via Ollama → Vault note with evidence.

## Requirements
- Pipeline must be triggerable manually via `node .opencode/plugins/run-review.js`.
- Git-Bash path on Windows: `C:/Program Files/Git/bin/bash.exe` (used quoted in pwsh).
- Evidence in Vault note: `verify.sh` stdout, exit code, reviewer answer/session ID.
- Note format: YAML frontmatter + sections Ergebnis/Schritt-Abgleich/Input-Output/verify.sh.
- Reviewer model configurable via `.env` variable `REVIEWER_MODEL` (default: `ollama/codellama:latest`).

## Decisions
- Manual entry point via `run-review.js` instead of `session.idle`.
- Reviewer call via Ollama HTTP API (`fetch("http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/generate")`) since the standalone Node script has no OpenCode SDK.
- Note name and `dateien` derived from `git status --porcelain`, filtered to `\.py$`.
- `REVIEWER_MODEL` read natively via `fs.readFileSync(DOTENV)` + regex.
- `verify.sh` invoked with argument `.` (`bash.exe scripts/verify.sh .`); log written to `verify-run.log` in workspace root.
- `verify.sh` uses git-changed-files mode (TARGET=`.` → `git status --porcelain`); fallback with `--ignore` list for explicit paths intact.
- Stray-scratch-files problem solved via `.gitignore` (not a filter in verify.sh): `check_api.py`, `inspect_db*.py`, `mini_beispiel.py`, `remove_duplicates.py`, `run_check.py`, `tmp_inspect_db.py` ignored → disappear from `git status`, git mode stays generic.
- Code-Mode `execute` tool cannot `require`/Node builtins → shell commands via `shell` tool.
- Exit-code check in pwsh: real exit code via `$LASTEXITCODE` (also behind `| Out-String`), not `echo "EXIT=$?"` (boolean True/False).
- Open strategy: pytest exit 5 ("no tests ran") to be treated as passed in verify.sh when changed .py files contain no doctests (not yet implemented).

## Work State
Break the objective into smaller goals and report which are completed, which are being worked on, and which are blocked.
### Completed
- `run-review.js` fully written and confirmed by Read (186 lines): native .env parsing, Ollama HTTP call (120 s timeout), verify.sh via Git Bash, note write to `codeguardian/`, CLI entry point, log to `.opencode/run-review.log`.
- Entry-check fix applied (basename comparison).
- `verify.sh` edited with git-changed-files mode (lines 17–29), fallback intact; full re-read confirmed.
- `python -m pytest --doctest-modules projects/csv2json/src/csv2json.py` runs cleanly (4 doctests); pytest 9.1.1.
- Ollama reachable: `http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/tags`, model `codellama:latest` present.
- `.gitignore` edit applied (6 root scratch files ignored) → stray-files problem solved.

- Commit status of `projects/csv2json/src/csv2json.py` checked: included in commit `14aa7e32`, working tree clean.

### Active
- **Ollama timeout fix**: raise run-review.js timeout (e.g. 300 s) and/or shorten review prompt; then re-run so the Vault note contains a real reviewer answer + session ID instead of an error section.
- **verify.sh exit 5**: pytest "no tests ran" — changed `scripts/__init__.py`/`scripts/check_providers.py` have no doctests → 0 collected → exit 5. Pipeline reads this as failure; fix missing (treat exit 5 as passed/skipped or only check doctest-bearing files); then revalidate with `$LASTEXITCODE` (expected 0).

### Blocked

## Next Move
1. `run-review.js`: raise Ollama timeout from 120 s to at least 300 s and/or shorten review prompt; re-run `node .opencode/plugins/run-review.js` → Vault note should contain real reviewer answer + session ID.

3. For real csv2json review path (file is committed, no longer in git status): explicit run `bash.exe scripts/verify.sh projects/csv2json/src/csv2json.py` or run-review.js with target.
4. Clean up artifact file `C：UsersDirkBielerAppDataLocalTempopencodeverify_run5.log` + `verify-run.log`.
5. OMNI-INBOX.md: set entry to `- [x]`, note solution.

- `E:\AI-System 3.0\.opencode\plugins\run-review.js`: trigger script (.env parsing, Ollama call with 120 s timeout, note write, logging) — timeout fix needed here next.
- `E:\AI-System 3.0\scripts\verify.sh`: pytest doctest runner; git mode (lines 17–29); needs exit-5 handling (currently `exit $?` propagates pytest exit 5 unchecked).

- Ollama call in run-review.js timed out after 120 s during E2E run (`The operation was aborted due to timeout`) — `codellama:latest` was ~36 s in benchmark for short prompts; full review prompt takes longer; timeout fix pending.
- Node warning during E2E run: `MODULE_TYPELESS_PACKAGE_JSON` — run-review.js parsed as ES module; optional `"type": "module"` in `.opencode/package.json` could be added.
- pytest exit codes: 5 = "no tests ran" — verify.sh line 27 `exit $?` propagates it; pipeline (exit ≠ 0 → "fehlgeschlagen") would misjudge it.
- After gitignore fix, `git status` shows only: ` M 00-Home/Index.md`, ` M OMNI-INBOX.md`, ` M opencode.json`, ` M scripts/verify.sh`, ` M .gitignore`, plus untracked: `scripts/__init__.py`, `scripts/check_providers.py`, `projects/code-guardian-engine/`, `projects/json2csv/`, `projects/tiktok-analysis/`, `projects/csv2json/src/__pycache__/`.
- Session shell is pwsh: `C:/Program Files/Git/bin/bash.exe` as a whole in quotes; Unix pipes only via `bash.exe -c "..."`; real exit code via `$LASTEXITCODE` (also behind `| Out-String`), not `echo "EXIT=$?"` (boolean True/False).
- Code-Mode `execute` runtime has no `require`/`fs`/`child_process` — use `shell` tool for shell calls.
- Full-repo pytest (`.`) blocks at collect on ffmpeg/av plugin imports (`code/video-analyse/`, `02_ECC/tests/`) — git mode avoids this.
- Python: `C:\Users\DirkBieler\AppData\Local\Programs\Python\Python312\python.exe`, pytest 9.1.1.

1. **verify.sh exit 5**: In der git-Mode-Branch (Zeile 26-27) läuft `python -m pytest ...` und `exit $?` propagiert exit 5. Ich muss exit 5 abfangen und als "Keine auswertbaren Doctests" mit exit 0 melden. Einfach: nach dem pytest-Aufruf Prüfung auf exit 5. Am besten: pytest-Ausführung in eine Variable, exit code prüfen.

   Da `set -e` läuft, kann ich nicht einfach `EXIT=$?` nach dem Aufruf machen — der Skript bricht vorher ab. Ich muss `set +e` temporarily oder `python ... || true` + `$?` auffangen. Einfachster Weg: `python -m pytest ...; EXIT_CODE=$?` mit `set +e` drum herum, oder `python ... || EXIT_CODE=$?`.

   Besser: `set +e` vorher, `python ...`, `EXIT_CODE=$?`, dann auf 5 prüfen.

   Oder: `if python -m pytest ...; then exit 0; elif [ $? -eq 5 ]; then echo "..."; exit 0; else exit $?; fi`. Aber mit `set -e` funktioniert `if`-Bedingung OK — der exit code innerhalb der Bedingung wird nicht als Fehler gewertet. Also:

   ```
   if python -m pytest --doctest-modules -v --tb=short --capture=no "${FILES[@]}"; then
     exit 0
   fi
   EXIT_CODE=$?
   if [ "$EXIT_CODE" -eq 5 ]; then
     echo "Keine auswertbaren Doctests in den geänderten Dateien (pytest exit 5) — als bestanden gewertet."
     exit 0
   fi
   exit "$EXIT_CODE"

## Objective
- Make the Codeguardian-Pipeline work end-to-end via manual trigger `run-review.js`: `verify.sh` → Reviewer-Agent via Ollama → Vault note with real evidence (answer + session ID).

## Requirements
- Pipeline triggerable via `node .opencode/plugins/run-review.js`.
- Git-Bash path: `C:/Program Files/Git/bin/bash.exe` (quoted in pwsh).
- Evidence in Vault note: verify.sh stdout, exit code, reviewer answer/session ID.
- Note format: YAML frontmatter + sections Ergebnis/Schritt-Abgleich/Input-Output/verify.sh.
- Reviewer model configurable via `.env` variable `REVIEWER_MODEL` (default: `ollama/codellama:latest`).

## Decisions
- Manual entry point via `run-review.js` instead of `session.idle`.
- Reviewer call via Ollama HTTP API (`fetch("http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/generate")`) — standalone Node script has no OpenCode SDK.
- Note name and `dateien` derived from `git status --porcelain`, filtered to `\.py$`.
- `REVIEWER_MODEL` parsed natively from `.env` via regex; `ollama/` prefix stripped before sending to Ollama.
- `verify.sh` invoked as `bash.exe scripts/verify.sh .`; log written to `verify-run.log` in workspace root.
- Stray-scratch-files problem solved via `.gitignore`.
- Ollama timeout raised from 120 s to 300 s (`AbortSignal.timeout(300_000)` at line 86 of `run-review.js`).
- **Exit-5 handling in verify.sh needs re-fix**: the `|| EXIT_CODE=$?` on a separate line does not capture pytest's exit correctly under `set -euo pipefail`. Must move the capture onto the same line as the pytest invocation (e.g. `pytest … "$TARGET"; EXIT_CODE=$?`).

## Work State
### Completed
- `run-review.js` fully written (ES module): native .env parsing, Ollama HTTP call, verify.sh via Git Bash, Vault note write to `codeguardian/`.
- Ollama timeout fix applied: line 86 = `AbortSignal.timeout(300_000)`.
- Exit-5 branch printed in verify.sh (lines 87–94), but **capture itself still broken** — exit 5 still emitted on full-repo run.
- Python pytest runs cleanly for csv2json module (4 doctests).
- Ollama reachable; model `codellama:latest` present.
- `.gitignore` edit applied — stray files ignored.
- First end-to-end run completed: diff detection worked, verify.sh produced exit=5, note written — contained only timeout error (pre-fix).

### Active
- Fix verify.sh exit-code capture: move `EXIT_CODE=$?` to same line as pytest call so pipefail doesn't swallow the real exit value.
- Revalidate: `bash.exe scripts/verify.sh .` → expect exit 0 (was 5 due to uncaptured pytest result).
- Re-run full pipeline `node .opencode/plugins/run-review.js` → new Vault note must contain real reviewer answer + session ID.
- For committed-module path (csv2json): explicit run `bash.exe scripts/verify.sh projects/csv2json/src/csv2json.py`.

### Blocked
- **verify.sh line ~83**: `pytest … "$TARGET" || EXIT_CODE=$?` on separate line does not retain pytest's non-zero exit under `set -euo pipefail`. Needs rewrite to `pytest … "$TARGET"; EXIT_CODE=$?` (or equivalent) before the if/elif block.

## Next Move
1. Rewrite verify.sh line ~83: change `"$TARGET" || EXIT_CODE=$?` (next line) to `"$TARGET"; EXIT_CODE=$?` on same line — this preserves the real exit code under pipefail.
2. Revalidate: `& "C:/Program Files/Git/bin/bash.exe" scripts/verify.sh .; echo "EXIT=$LASTEXITCODE"` → expect `EXIT=0`.
3. Re-run: `node .opencode/plugins/run-review.js` → confirm new Vault note contains real reviewer answer + session ID (not timeout error, not exit-5 placeholder).
4. If csv2json path needed: `& "C:/Program Files/Git/bin/bash.exe" scripts/verify.sh projects/csv2json/src/csv2json.py`.
5. Clean stale logs: remove `verify-run.log` and temp artifacts if still present.
6. Update `OMNI-INBOX.md`: set entry to `- [x]`, note solution.

## Relevant Files
- `E:\AI-System 3.0\.opencode\plugins\run-review.js`: trigger script; timeout 300_000 at line 86; Ollama call; note writer.
- `E:\AI-System 3.0\scripts\verify.sh`: exit-code capture bug at line ~83; exit-5 branch at lines 87–95.
- `E:\AI-System 3.0\codeguardian\PRUEFUNG-2026-11-11T15-18-45.md`: example Vault note (timeout error — pre-fix run).
- `E:\AI-System 3.0\projects\csv2json\src\csv2json.py`: target module with 4 doctests; committed at `14aa7e32`.
- `E:\AI-System 3.0\.gitignore`: 6 root scratch files ignored.
- `E:\AI-System 3.0\.env`: `REVIEWER_MODEL=ollama/codellama:latest`.
- `E:\AI-System 3.0\OMNI-INBOX.md`: inbox entry to close once pipeline passes.
- `E:\AI-System 3.0\verify-run.log`: stale log from old run — cleanup candidate.

## Important Context
- Ollama benchmark: `codellama:latest` ~36 s short prompts; full review prompt exceeded 120 s → timeout now 300 s.
- `set -euo pipefail` means any un-captured non-zero exit aborts the script — `|| EC=$?` on the **next** line does NOT save you under pipefail because the sub-shell/status chain behaves differently in git-bash on Windows.
- Full-repo pytest (`.`) blocks at collect on ffmpeg/av plugin imports — git mode (`--staged` / changed-files filter) avoids this.
- Session shell is pwsh: invoke bash with whole path quoted: `& "C:/Program Files/Git/bin/bash.exe" scripts/verify.sh .`.
- Node warning during E2E run: `MODULE_TYPELESS_PACKAGE_JSON` — optional fix: add `"type": "module"` to `.opencode/package.json`.

## Objective
Make the Codeguardian-Pipeline work end-to-end via manual trigger `run-review.js`: `verify.sh` → Reviewer-Agent via Ollama → Vault note with real evidence (reviewer answer + session ID).

## Requirements
- Pipeline triggerable via `node .opencode/plugins/run-review.js`.
- Git-Bash path: `C:/Program Files/Git/bin/bash.exe` (quoted in pwsh).
- Evidence in Vault note: verify.sh stdout, exit code, reviewer answer/session ID.
- Note format: YAML frontmatter + sections Ergebnis/Schritt-Abgleich/Input-Output/verify.sh.
- Reviewer model configurable via `.env` variable `REVIEWER_MODEL` (default: `ollama/codellama:latest`).

## Decisions
- Manual entry point via `run-review.js` instead of `session.idle`.
- Reviewer call via Ollama HTTP API (`fetch("http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/generate")`) — standalone Node script has no OpenCode SDK.
- Note name and `dateien` derived from `git status --porcelain`, filtered to `\.py$`.
- `REVIEWER_MODEL` parsed natively from `.env` via regex; `ollama/` prefix stripped before sending to Ollama.
- `verify.sh` invoked as `bash.exe scripts/verify.sh .`; log written to `verify-run.log` in workspace root.
- Stray-scratch-files problem solved via `.gitignore`.
- Ollama timeout raised from 120 s to 300 s (`AbortSignal.timeout(300_000)` at line 86 of `run-review.js`).

## Work State
### Completed
- `run-review.js` fully written (ES module): native .env parsing, Ollama HTTP call, verify.sh via Git Bash, Vault note write to `codeguardian/`.

## Objective
Make the Codeguardian-Pipeline work end-to-end via manual trigger `run-review.js` — verify.sh → Reviewer-Agent (Ollama) → Vault note with real evidence AND proper, clean structure.

## Requirements
- Pipeline triggerable via `node .opencode/plugins/run-review.js`.
- Evidence in Vault note: verify.sh stdout, exit code, reviewer answer + session ID.
- Note format: YAML frontmatter + sections `Ergebnis` / `Schritt-Abgleich` / `Input-Output` / `verify.sh`.
- Reviewer model configurable via `.env` variable `REVIEWER_MODEL` (default: `ollama/codellama:latest`).
- NEW: Note must be clean — no raw reviewer preamble, no embedded reviewer YAML block, no `undefined`, no missing sections.

## Decisions
- Manual entry point via `run-review.js` (no `session.idle`).
- Reviewer call via Ollama HTTP API (`fetch("http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/generate")`); `ollama/` prefix stripped; `REVIEWER_MODEL` parsed natively from `.env`.
- Note name + `dateien` from `git status --porcelain`, filtered to `\.py$` (flaw: raw porcelain prefix `?? ` leaked into `dateien` entries — fix should use `awk '{print $2}'` style path extraction).
- `verify.sh` invoked via quoted `C:/Program Files/Git/bin/bash.exe`; Ollama timeout 300 s.
- verify.sh exit-5 fix: `|| EXIT_CODE=$?` capture + exit-5→0 branch (verified: `EXIT=0`).
- Root cause of dirty note: reviewer prompt asks the model to "create a structured Obsidian note" → model returns preamble + complete note (own YAML block, headings) and run-review.js embeds it raw. Fix planned in `run-review.js`: sanitize/restructure answer or constrain prompt to a strict answer format.

## Work State
### Completed
- `run-review.js` fully written and running end-to-end (ES module; .env parsing, Ollama HTTP call, verify.sh via Git Bash, note writer); full file (186 lines) now inspected — config/helpers lines 1–31 confirmed, remaining structure to be located in-line while fixing.
- Ollama timeout 300 s in place; call succeeds (~80,7 s, within timeout).
- verify.sh exit-5 fix in git branch verified: `bash.exe scripts/verify.sh .` → `EXIT=0` (2 changed `.py` files, 0 doctests → skip message).
- Full pipeline run: `node .opencode/plugins/run-review.js` → verify.sh exit=0 → reviewer note `PRUEFUNG-2026-11-11T15-55-45.md` written with real answer + session.
- `.gitignore` edit applied (stray scratch files ignored).

### Active

1. Fix note generation in `run-review.js`: sanitize reviewer answer (remove `---…---` YAML block, leading preamble), parse test count from verify.sh output for `Ergebnis`, keep/fill all sections; optionally tighten the reviewer prompt to demand a strict German answer format.
2. Re-run `node .opencode/plugins/run-review.js` → confirm clean note in `codeguardian/`.

In edit #2 I wrote `[SCHRIITT-ABGLEICH]` in the prompt. In edit #3 I wrote the section regex looking for `(?:SCHRIITT-ABGLEICH|INPUT-OUTPUT|ABWEICHUNGEN)`, and I'm calling `section("SCHRIITT-ABGLEICH")`. Let me check the recent context.

Edit #3 oldString/newString:
```
const section = (name) => {
    const m = reviewResult.match(new RegExp(`\\[${name}\\]([\\s\\S]*?)(?=\\[(?:SCHRIITT-ABGLEICH|INPUT-OUTPUT|ABWEICHUNGEN)\\]|$)`));
    return m ? m[1].trim() : "";
  };
  const schritt = section("SCHRIITT-ABGLEICH") || "Schritt-Kommentare konnten nicht abgeglichen werden.";
```

And edit #2's prompt has `[SCHRIITT-ABGLEICH]`. So at least they're consistent with each other (both use SCHRIITT-ABGLEICH). But that's a typo — "Schritt" is spelled with a single T in the middle: S-C-H-R-I-T-T. So the correct German would be `[SCHRIITT-ABGLEICH]`... wait: "Schritt" = S-c-h-r-i-t-t. Uppercase: SCHRIIT? No! Uppercase of "Schritt" is "SCHRITT". Let me spell it out: S, c, h, r, i, t, t → uppercase: S, C, H, R, I, T, T = "SCHRITT". So the correct marker should be `[SCHRITT-ABGLEICH]`.

In my edits I wrote `SCHRIITT-ABGLEICH` — that's S-C-H-R-I-I-T-T, with an extra I! That's a typo ("Schriitt" instead of "Schritt"). But the important thing is: is it consistent between the prompt (edit #2) and the extractor (edit #3)? Edit #2's prompt: `[SCHRIITT-ABGLEICH]`. Edit #3's regex: `(?:SCHRIITT-ABGLEICH|INPUT-OUTPUT|ABWEICHUNGEN)` and `section("SCHRIITT-ABGLEICH")`. So both use the typo'd form — it's internally consistent, so extraction will work. But it's ugly and a potential source of confusion. If the model outputs `[SCHRITT-ABGLEICH]` (correct spelling), the regex won't match and the section will fall back to "Schritt-Kommentare konnten nicht abgeglichen werden." — even though the model did answer, we'd lose the content.

A weak model like codellama is likely to follow the prompt exactly (copy the marker verbatim), so consistency is mostly fine. But to be safe, the regex should accept both spellings. Let me read the current state of the file and fix it robustly.

Also, there might be other issues:

1. `randomUUID()` — need to check whether it's imported. The original file had `import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto"`. According to the checkpoint, config/helpers were verified at lines 1–31. I should re-read the entire file to check current state.

2. `fs` — edit #3 uses `fs.readdirSync`. Need to check whether `fs` is imported (probably `import fs from "node:fs"` or `import * as fs from "node:fs"`). Also `mkdir` and `writeFile` are probably from `node:fs/promises`. And `path`.

3. `reviewResult` variable — the note writer references `reviewResult` — need to check that the variable for the Ollama response is named `reviewResult` in the current file.

4. `datum` — defined in edit #2's block: `const datum = new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 19);` Good, ISO format without milliseconds, e.g., `2026-11-11T15:55:45`. Note name: `PRUEFUNG-${datum.replace(/[:.]/g, "-")}.md` → `PRUEFUNG-2026-11-11T15-55-45.md`. Good.

5. `durchlauf` — counts existing notes + 1. Fine.

6. `section()` regex: `new RegExp(`\\[${name}\\]([\\s\\S]*?)(?=\\[(?:SCHRIITT-ABGLEICH|INPUT-OUTPUT|ABWEICHUNGEN)\\]|$)`)`. There's a subtle bug here: lazy `[\s\S]*?` with lookahead `(?=\[...?\]|$)` — the `$` in JS regex without the `m` flag only matches end of string. Since the lazy match tries to expand as needed, the regex engine will match up to the next marker or end of string. Actually wait, with lazy `[\s\S]*?`, the regex engine tries to expand as needed. The lookahead checks whether the next position is `[SCHRITT...]` or end of string. At each position, if it's not end of string and not a marker, the lazy match expands. So it stops at the first marker or end of string. That works.

But there's an edge case: what if the model wraps the marker in backticks or bold? Unlikely. Also, what if the model uses lowercase markers or omits the brackets? Fallback text applies. OK.

Another subtle point: if the model outputs the marker as `[SCHRIITT-ABGLEICH]` — no problem. But what if the model outputs `[SCHRITT-ABGLEICH]` (correct spelling)? The section for "SCHRIITT-ABGLEICH" would be... wait, `section("SCHRIITT-ABGLEICH")` searches for `\[SCHRIITT-ABGLEICH\]` — not found → returns "" → falls back to default. And the model's content under `[SCHRITT-ABGLEICH]` would be lost. To make it robust, the regex should accept both: `SCHRI?IT?T`... simpler: use `(?:SCHRI?TT|SCHRIITT|SCHRITT)` or a case-insensitive regex with pattern `SCHR(I+)?T-ABGLEICH`. Let me use a case-insensitive regex and pattern `\\[(?:SCHRI?TT|SCHRIT|SCHRIIT|SCHRIITT)-ABGLEICH\\]`. Hmm, getting complex. Simpler: define a const `SCHRITT_ALT = "SCHR(I*)T-ABGLEICH"`... let me think.

Actually, the simplest and most robust approach: normalize the review result before parsing — uppercase it? No, that breaks the German content.

Alternative: make the section regex case-insensitive and tolerant: for the Schrittabgleich marker, `\\[(?:SCHRIT|SCHRIITT|SCHRITT|SCHRIIT)-ABGLEICH\\]`. German "Schritt" = SCHRIIT? No. Let me spell it out very carefully:

7. Also, potential issue: the model might answer with markers but also include text before the first marker (preamble). Since I'm extracting by markers, the preamble just gets ignored. Good — that's the robust design.

8. `testInfo` — good, no more `undefined`.

## Objective
Make the Codeguardian-Pipeline work end-to-end via manual trigger `run-review.js` — verify.sh → Reviewer-Agent (Ollama) → Vault note with real evidence AND proper, clean structure.

## Requirements
- Pipeline triggerable via `node .opencode/plugins/run-review.js`.
- Evidence in Vault note: verify.sh stdout, exit code, reviewer answer + session ID.
- Note format: YAML frontmatter + sections `Ergebnis` / `Schritt-Abgleich` / `Input/Output` / `verify.sh`.
- Reviewer model configurable via `.env` variable `REVIEWER_MODEL` (default: `ollama/codellama:latest`).
- Note must be clean — no raw reviewer preamble, no embedded reviewer YAML block, no `undefined`, no missing sections, no `?? ` prefixed `dateien` entries.

## Decisions
- Manual entry point via `run-review.js` (no `session.idle`).
- Reviewer call via Ollama HTTP API (`fetch("http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/generate")`); `ollama/` prefix stripped; `REVIEWER_MODEL` parsed natively from `.env`.
- `dateien` from `git status --porcelain`, filtered to `\.py$`.
- `verify.sh` invoked via quoted `C:/Program Files/Git/bin/bash.exe`; Ollama timeout 300 s.
- verify.sh exit-5 fix: `|| EXIT_CODE=$?` capture + exit-5→0 branch (verified: `EXIT=0`).
- Root cause of dirty note: reviewer prompt asked the model to "create a structured Obsidian note" → model returned preamble + own YAML + `undefined` (from `match(/(\d+) passed/)?.[1]` returning null). Fix: build note structure in JS, constrain model to strict marker format.
- Three fixes applied to `run-review.js`: (1) `getChangedPythonFiles`: `.slice(3).trim()` instead of regex (strips `?? ` prefix); (2) reviewer prompt rewritten to demand exactly three markers `[SCHRIITT-ABGLEICH]` / `[INPUT-OUTPUT]` / `[ABWEICHUNGEN]`, German, no intro, no YAML, no extra headings; (3) note writer rewritten to extract sections from markers via regex, compute `testInfo` from verify.sh output, `abweichCount` from reviewer content, `durchlauf` from existing `PRUEFUNG-*.md` files, fill all required sections.

## Work State
### Completed
- `run-review.js` fully written (229 lines, ES module); re-read this session and confirmed: config constants (`VAULT_DIR`, `DOTENV`, `LOG_FILE=E:/AI-System 3.0/.opencode/run-review.log`), native `.env` parsing of `REVIEWER_MODEL` with quote-stripping and fallback default, `log()` helper appending to LOG_FILE via `execSync` echo on cmd shell.
- All three note-cleaning fixes applied in `run-review.js`.
- Ollama timeout 300 s in place; previous call succeeded (~80.7 s, within timeout).
- verify.sh exit-5 fix verified in branch: `bash.exe scripts/verify.sh .` → `EXIT=0` (2 changed `.py` files, 0 doctests → skip message).
- Full pipeline run previously produced `PRUEFUNG-2026-11-11T15-55-45.md` with real answer + session (but dirty — dirtyness now fixed in code, pending re-run confirmation).
- `.gitignore` edit applied (stray scratch files ignored).

## Objective
Make the Codeguardian-Pipeline work end-to-end via manual trigger `run-review.js` — verify.sh → Reviewer-Agent (Ollama) → Vault note with real evidence AND proper, clean structure.

## Requirements
- Pipeline triggerable via `node .opencode/plugins/run-review.js`.
- Evidence in Vault note: verify.sh stdout, exit code, reviewer answer + session ID.
- Note format: YAML frontmatter + sections `Ergebnis` / `Schritt-Abgleich` / `Input/Output` / `verify.sh`.
- Reviewer model configurable via `.env` variable `REVIEWER_MODEL` (default: `ollama/codellama:latest`).
- Note must be clean — no raw reviewer preamble, no embedded reviewer YAML block, no `undefined`, no missing sections, no `?? ` prefixed `dateien` entries.

## Decisions
- Manual entry point via `run-review.js` (no `session.idle`).
- Reviewer call via Ollama HTTP API (`fetch("http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/generate")`); `ollama/` prefix stripped; `REVIEWER_MODEL` parsed natively from `.env`.
- `dateien` from `git status --porcelain`, filtered to `\.py$`.
- `verify.sh` invoked via quoted `C:/Program Files/Git/bin/bash.exe`; Ollama timeout 300 s.
- verify.sh exit-5 fix: `|| EXIT_CODE=$?` capture + exit-5→0 branch (verified: `EXIT=0`).
- Root cause of dirty note: reviewer prompt asked the model to "create a structured Obsidian note" → model returned preamble + own YAML + `undefined` (from `match(/(\d+) passed/)?.[1]` returning null). Fix: build note structure in JS, constrain model to strict marker format.
- Three fixes applied to `run-review.js`: (1) `getChangedPythonFiles`: `.slice(3).trim()` instead of regex (strips `?? ` prefix); (2) reviewer prompt rewritten to demand exactly three markers `[SCHRIITT-ABGLEICH]` / `[INPUT-OUTPUT]` / `[ABWEICHUNGEN]`, German, no intro, no YAML, no extra headings; (3) note writer rewritten to extract sections from markers via regex, compute `testInfo` from verify.sh output, `abweichCount` from reviewer content, `durchlauf` from existing `PRUEFUNG-*.md` files, fill all required sections.

## Work State
### Completed
- `run-review.js` fully written (229 lines, ES module); re-read this session and confirmed: config constants (`VAULT_DIR`, `DOTENV`, `LOG_FILE=E:/AI-System 3.0/.opencode/run-review.log`), native `.env` parsing of `REVIEWER_MODEL` with quote-stripping and fallback default, `log()` helper appending to LOG_FILE via `execSync` echo on cmd shell.
- All three note-cleaning fixes applied in `run-review.js`.
- Ollama timeout 300 s in place; previous call succeeded (~80.7 s, within timeout).
- verify.sh exit-5 fix verified in branch: `bash.exe scripts/verify.sh .` → `EXIT=0` (2 changed `.py` files, 0 doctests → skip message).
- Full pipeline run previously produced `PRUEFUNG-2026-11-11T15-55-45.md` with real answer + session (but dirty — dirtyness now fixed in code, pending re-run confirmation).
- `.gitignore` edit applied (stray scratch files ignored).
- Confirmed untracked `.py` files: `scripts/__init__.py`, `scripts/check_providers.py`.
- Confirmed 8 existing `PRUEFUNG-*.md` notes in `codeguardian/` (oldest `PRUEFUNG-nvidia-provider-minute-cap-2026-11-10T00-00-00.md`, newest `PRUEFUNG-2026-11-11T15-55-45.md`).
- Confirmed stray corrupted file location: repo root `E:\AI-System 3.0\C?UsersDirkBielerAppDataLocalTempopencodeverify_run5.log` (159084 bytes, 11.11.2026 03:06:37) — a mangled temp path written to the working dir, not actually in Temp.

### Active
- Re-run `node .opencode/plugins/run-review.js` to confirm clean note structure after the three code fixes.
- Verify the reviewer actually returns the three markers (model is weak on structure — code-side marker extraction is the reliable fix).

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run `node .opencode/plugins/run-review.js` → confirm clean note in `codeguardian/` (no preamble, no embedded YAML, no `undefined`, all sections present, clean `dateien` paths).
2. Clean stale artifacts: `E:\AI-System 3.0\verify-run.log` and the stray root file `E:\AI-System 3.0\C?UsersDirkBielerAppDataLocalTempopencodeverify_run5.log`.
3. Update `OMNI-INBOX.md` codeguardian entry to `- [x]` + solution (open entries like BotFather `/revoke` out of scope).

- `E:\AI-System 3.0\.opencode\plugins\run-review.js`: trigger + note writer; 229 lines; all three fixes applied here.
- `E:\AI-System 3.0\codeguardian\PRUEFUNG-2026-11-11T15-55-45.md`: latest dirty note (pre-fix) — reference for the raw-answer problem.
- `E:\AI-System 3.0\scripts\verify.sh`: fixed with `|| EXIT_CODE=$?` capture + exit-5→0; working, uncommitted.
- `E:\AI-System 3.0\.env`: `REVIEWER_MODEL=ollama/codellama:latest`.
- `E:\AI-System 3.0\OMNI-INBOX.md`: codeguardian entry to close.
- `E:\AI-System 3.0\verify-run.log`: stale log from old run — cleanup candidate.
- `E:\AI-System 3.0\C?UsersDirkBielerAppDataLocalTempopencodeverify_run5.log`: stray corrupted-path artifact at repo root — cleanup candidate.

- Session shell is pwsh: invoke bash as `& "C:/Program Files/Git/bin/bash.exe" scripts/verify.sh .`.
- Code Mode `execute` tool: `require` unavailable (ESM-only runtime) — failed with `ReferenceError: Unknown identifier 'require'`; use `import` or the `shell` tool for state inspection instead.
- pytest exit codes: 0 OK, 1 failed, 5 no tests collected; `set -euo pipefail` makes a bare failing pytest abort verify.sh (hence `|| EXIT_CODE=$?` pattern).
- Uncommitted: `00-Home/Index.md`, `OMNI-INBOX.md`, `opencode.json`, `scripts/verify.sh`, `.gitignore`; untracked: `scripts/__init__.py`, `scripts/check_providers.py`, project folders, `verify-run.log`, plus pre-existing scratch files (e.g. `-test-parser.ps1`, `-tsc-raw.txt`) and 0-byte `eradication_*.log` files at root.

- `.opencode/package.json` lacks `"type": "module"` → Node MODULE_TYPELESS warning on every run (cosmetic).
- Ollama reachable; `codellama:latest` present; ~80 s answer fits 300 s timeout; model is weak on structure — expect it to ignore format constraints, so code-side sanitizing is the reliable fix.

## Objective
Make the Codeguardian-Pipeline work end-to-end via manual trigger `run-review.js` — verify.sh → Reviewer-Agent (Ollama) → Vault note with real evidence and a clean, well-formed structure.

## Requirements
- Pipeline triggerable via `node .opencode/plugins/run-review.js`.
- Evidence in Vault note: verify.sh stdout, exit code, reviewer answer + session ID.
- Note format: YAML frontmatter + sections `Ergebnis` / `Schritt-Abgleich` / `Input/Output` / `verify.sh`.
- Reviewer model configurable via `.env` variable `REVIEWER_MODEL` (default: `ollama/codellama:latest`).
- Note must be clean: no raw reviewer preamble, no embedded reviewer YAML block, no `undefined`, no missing sections, no `?? ` prefixed `dateien` entries.

## Decisions
- Manual entry point via `run-review.js` (no `session.idle` trigger).
- Reviewer call via Ollama HTTP API (`fetch("http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/generate")`); `ollama/` prefix stripped; `REVIEWER_MODEL` parsed natively from `.env`.
- `dateien` from `git status --porcelain`, filtered to `\.py$`.
- verify.sh invoked via quoted `C:/Program Files/Git/bin/bash.exe`; Ollama timeout 300 s.
- verify.sh exit-5 fix: `|| EXIT_CODE=$?` capture + exit-5→0 branch (verified: `EXIT=0`).
- Root cause of dirty note: reviewer prompt asked the model to "create a structured Obsidian note" → model returned preamble + own YAML + `undefined` (from `match(/(\d+) passed/)?.[1]` returning null). Fix: build note structure in JS, constrain model to strict marker format.

## Objective
Make the Codeguardian-Pipeline work end-to-end via manual trigger `run-review.js` — verify.sh → Reviewer-Agent (Ollama) → Vault note with real evidence and a clean, well-formed structure.

## Requirements
- Pipeline triggerable via `node .opencode/plugins/run-review.js`.
- Evidence in Vault note: verify.sh stdout, exit code, reviewer answer + session ID.
- Note format: YAML frontmatter + sections `Ergebnis` / `Schritt-Abgleich` / `Input/Output` / `verify.sh`.
- Reviewer model configurable via `.env` variable `REVIEWER_MODEL` (default: `ollama/codellama:latest`).
- Note must be clean: no raw reviewer preamble, no embedded reviewer YAML block, no `undefined`, no missing sections, no `?? ` prefixed `dateien` entries.

## Decisions
- Manual entry point via `run-review.js` (no `session.idle` trigger).
- Reviewer call via Ollama HTTP API (`fetch("http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/generate")`); `ollama/` prefix stripped; `REVIEWER_MODEL` parsed natively from `.env`.
- `dateien` from `git status --porcelain`, filtered to `\.py$`.
- verify.sh invoked via quoted `C:/Program Files/Git/bin/bash.exe`; Ollama timeout 300 s.
- verify.sh exit-5 fix: `|| EXIT_CODE=$?` capture + exit-5→0 branch (verified: `EXIT=0`).
- Root cause of dirty note: reviewer prompt asked the model to "create a structured Obsidian note" → model returned preamble + own YAML + `undefined` (from `match(/(\d+) passed/)?.[1]` returning null). Fix: build note structure in JS, constrain model to strict marker format.
- Three fixes applied to `run-review.js`: (1) `getChangedPythonFiles`: `.slice(3).trim()` instead of regex (strips `?? ` prefix); (2) reviewer prompt rewritten to demand exactly three markers `[SCHRIITT-ABGLEICH]` / `[INPUT-OUTPUT]` / `[ABWEICHUNGEN]`, German, no intro, no YAML, no extra headings; (3) note writer rewritten to extract sections from markers via regex, compute `testInfo` from verify.sh output, `abweichCount` from reviewer content, `durchlauf` from existing `PRUEFUNG-*.md` files, fill all required sections.

- `run-review.js` fully written (229 lines, ES module) with all three note-cleaning fixes; re-read and confirmed: config constants (`VAULT_DIR`, `DOTENV`, `LOG_FILE=E:/AI-System 3.0/.opencode/run-review.log`), native `.env` parsing of `REVIEWER_MODEL` with quote-stripping and fallback default, `log()` helper appending to LOG_FILE via `execSync` echo on cmd shell.

## Objective
Make the Codeguardian-Pipeline work end-to-end via manual trigger `run-review.js` — verify.sh → Reviewer-Agent (Ollama) → Vault note with real evidence and a clean, well-formed structure.

## Requirements
- Pipeline triggerable via `node .opencode/plugins/run-review.js`.
- Evidence in Vault note: verify.sh stdout, exit code, reviewer answer + session ID.
- Note format: YAML frontmatter + sections `Ergebnis` / `Schritt-Abgleich` / `Input/Output` / `verify.sh`.
- Reviewer model configurable via `.env` variable `REVIEWER_MODEL` (default: `ollama/codellama:latest`).
- Note must be clean: no raw reviewer preamble, no embedded reviewer YAML block, no `undefined`, no missing sections, no `?? ` prefixed `dateien` entries.

## Decisions
- Manual entry point via `run-review.js` (no `session.idle` trigger).
- Reviewer call via Ollama HTTP API (`fetch("http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/generate")`); `ollama/` prefix stripped; `REVIEWER_MODEL` parsed natively from `.env`.
- `dateien` from `git status --porcelain`, filtered to `\.py$`.
- verify.sh invoked via quoted `C:/Program Files/Git/bin/bash.exe`; Ollama timeout 300 s.
- verify.sh exit-5 fix: `|| EXIT_CODE=$?` capture + exit-5→0 branch.
- Root cause of dirty note: reviewer prompt asked model to "create a structured Obsidian note" → model returned preamble + own YAML + `undefined`. Fix: build note structure in JS, constrain model to strict marker format.
- Three fixes in `run-review.js`: (1) `getChangedPythonFiles`: `.slice(3).trim()` instead of regex; (2) reviewer prompt rewritten to demand exactly three markers `[SCHRIITT-ABGLEICH]` / `[INPUT-OUTPUT]` / `[ABWEICHUNGEN]`, German, no intro, no YAML, no extra headings; (3) note writer rewritten to extract sections from markers, compute `testInfo` from verify.sh output, `abweichCount` from reviewer content, `durchlauf` from existing `PRUEFUNG-*.md` files.
- Confirmed after clean re-run (Lauf 9, `PRUEFUNG-2026-11-11T16-36-17.md`): reviewer content hallucination (codellama invents "missing imports") is a model weakness, not a pipeline bug — code-side marker extraction + sanitizing is the reliable layer.

- `run-review.js` fully written (229 lines, ES module) with all three note-cleaning fixes; config constants (`VAULT_DIR`, `DOTENV`, `LOG_FILE=E:/AI-System 3.0/.opencode/run-review.log`), native `.env` parsing of `REVIEWER_MODEL` with quote-stripping and fallback default, `log()` helper appending to LOG_FILE.

## Objective
Make the Codeguardian-Pipeline work end-to-end via manual trigger `run-review.js` — verify.sh → Reviewer-Agent (Ollama) → Vault note with real evidence and a clean, well-formed structure.

## Requirements
- Pipeline triggerable via `node .opencode/plugins/run-review.js`.
- Evidence in Vault note: verify.sh stdout, exit code, reviewer answer + session ID.
- Note format: YAML frontmatter + sections `Ergebnis` / `Schritt-Abgleich` / `Input/Output` / `verify.sh`.
- Reviewer model configurable via `.env` variable `REVIEWER_MODEL` (default: `ollama/codellama:latest`).
- Note must be clean: no raw reviewer preamble, no embedded reviewer YAML block, no `undefined`, no missing sections, no `?? ` prefixed `dateien` entries.

## Decisions
- Manual entry point via `run-review.js` (no `session.idle` trigger).
- Reviewer call via Ollama HTTP API (`fetch("http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/generate")`); `ollama/` prefix stripped; `REVIEWER_MODEL` parsed natively from `.env`.
- `dateien` from `git status --porcelain`, filtered to `\.py$`.
- verify.sh invoked via quoted `C:/Program Files/Git/bin/bash.exe`; Ollama timeout 300 s.
- verify.sh exit-5 fix: `|| EXIT_CODE=$?` capture + exit-5→0 branch.
- Root cause of dirty note: reviewer prompt asked model to "create a structured Obsidian note" → model returned preamble + own YAML + `undefined`. Fix: build note structure in JS, constrain model to strict marker format.

## Objective
- Make the Codeguardian-Pipeline work end-to-end via manual trigger `run-review.js` — verify.sh → Reviewer-Agent (Ollama) → Vault note with real evidence and a clean, well-formed structure.

## Requirements
- Pipeline triggerable via `node .opencode/plugins/run-review.js`.
- Evidence in Vault note: verify.sh stdout, exit code, reviewer answer + session ID.
- Note format: YAML frontmatter + sections `Ergebnis` / `Schritt-Abgleich` / `Input/Output` / `verify.sh`.
- Reviewer model configurable via `.env` variable `REVIEWER_MODEL` (default: `ollama/codellama:latest`).
- Note must be clean: no raw reviewer preamble, no embedded reviewer YAML block, no `undefined`, no missing sections, no `?? ` prefixed `dateien` entries.

## Decisions
- Manual entry point via `run-review.js` (no `session.idle` trigger).
- Reviewer call via Ollama HTTP API (`fetch("http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/generate")`); `ollama/` prefix stripped; `REVIEWER_MODEL` parsed natively from `.env`.
- `dateien` from `git status --porcelain`, filtered to `\.py$`.
- verify.sh invoked via quoted `C:/Program Files/Git/bin/bash.exe`; Ollama timeout 300 s.
- verify.sh exit-5 fix: `|| EXIT_CODE=$?` capture + exit-5→0 branch.

## Objective
- Make the Codeguardian-Pipeline work end-to-end via manual trigger `run-review.js` — verify.sh → Reviewer-Agent (Ollama) → Vault note with real evidence and a clean, well-formed structure.

## Requirements
- Pipeline triggerable via `node .opencode/plugins/run-review.js`.
- Evidence in Vault note: verify.sh stdout, exit code, reviewer answer + session ID.
- Note format: YAML frontmatter + sections `Ergebnis` / `Schritt-Abgleich` / `Input/Output` / `verify.sh`.
- Reviewer model configurable via `.env` variable `REVIEWER_MODEL` (default: `ollama/codellama:latest`).
- Note must be clean: no raw reviewer preamble, no embedded reviewer YAML block, no `undefined`, no missing sections, no `?? ` prefixed `dateien` entries.

## Decisions
- Manual entry point via `run-review.js` (no `session.idle` trigger).
- Reviewer call via Ollama HTTP API (`fetch("http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/generate")`); `ollama/` prefix stripped; `REVIEWER_MODEL` parsed natively from `.env`.
- `dateien` from `git status --porcelain`, filtered to `\.py$`.
- verify.sh invoked via quoted `C:/Program Files/Git/bin/bash.exe`; Ollama timeout 300 s.
- verify.sh exit-5 fix: `|| EXIT_CODE=$?` capture + exit-5→0 branch.
- Root cause of dirty note: reviewer prompt asked model to "create a structured Obsidian note" → model returned preamble + own YAML + `undefined`. Fix: build note structure in JS, constrain model to strict marker format.
- Three fixes in `run-review.js`: (1) `getChangedPythonFiles`: `.slice(3).trim()` instead of regex; (2) reviewer prompt rewritten to demand exactly three markers `[SCHRIITT-ABGLEICH]` / `[INPUT-OUTPUT]` / `[ABWEICHUNGEN]`, German, no intro, no YAML, no extra headings; (3) note writer rewritten to extract sections from markers, compute `testInfo` from verify.sh output, `abweichCount` from reviewer content, `durchlauf` from existing `PRUEFUNG-*.md` files.
- Reviewer content hallucination (codellama invents "missing imports") accepted as model weakness, not pipeline bug — code-side marker extraction + sanitizing is the reliable layer; no further prompt-level investment.
- Cleanup decided: stale root logs deleted; unrelated open BotFather entry in inbox left untouched.

## Objective
Post-Commit-Statuscheck auf Branch `freellmapi-isolated` abschließen:Vault-Struktur committen, Scratch-Dateien ignorieren lassen, `00-Home/Index.md` updaten.

## Requirements
- `.env` bleibt ignoriert.
- Conventional Commits auf Deutsch.
- Windows-Kompatibilität (`verify.py` statt `verify.sh`).
- Nur relevante Vault-/Codebestandteile versionieren; Scratch/Probe-Dateien ignorieren.

## Decisions
- Vault-Ordner (`00_Dashboard/`, `01_Projekte/`, `02_Agents/`, `02_ECC/`, `03_Skills/`, `06_Entscheidungen/`, `07_Recherche/`, `09_Prompts/`, `10_Wissensdatenbank/`, `AI-Content-Studio/`, `Bootstrap/`, `codeguardian/`, `Fehler/`, `INFO-Logs/`, `Projekte/`, `Templates/`, `agency-agents/`, `checkpoints/`, `code/`) werden versioniert.
- Scratch-Dateien (`_probe-videos.js`, `_scan-videos.js`, `_video-list.csv`, `_video-meta.csv`, `check.js`, `check-status.js`, `check_api.ps1`, `clean_projects.ps1`, `calendar.json`, `Modelfile.coder3b`, `Modelfile.fast`) bleiben unversioniert und erhalten `.gitignore`-Regeln.
- Telegram-Bot-Token `8836415662:…` bleibt im Repo (Boss-Beschluss).

## Work State
### Completed
- `.opencode/`-Pipeline committet (`45de29e9`).
- `auto-review.js` → `verify.py` Fix committet (`0525c0ec`).
- `AGENTS.md`, `AI-System-Core.md`, `EXECUTION_LOOP.md`, `.ecc/test-task/` committet.
- `verify.py` erstellt, Exit 5 bei leerem Target = erwartet.
- `.gitignore` erweitert (+ venv/cache/legacy/scratch-Regeln).
- `.gitignore` + `OMNI-INBOX.md` committet (`ea56029a`).

### Active
- Vault-Ordner per `git add` in Index bringen — vorheriger Befehl mit `\`-Continuation auf PowerShell fehlgeschlagen.
- Neue `.gitignore`-Regeln für Scratch-Dateien hinzufügen und committen.
- `00-Home/Index.md` um Codeguardian-Dashboard-Link ergänzen und committen.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. `git add` für alle zu versionierenden Vault-Ordner mit korrektem PowerShell-Syntax ausführen.
2. `.gitignore` um Scratch-Regeln erweitern (`_probe-*.js`, `_scan-*.js`, `*_list.csv`, `*_meta.csv`, `check*.js`, `check*.ps1`, `calendar.json`, `Modelfile.*`) und committen.
3. `00-Home/Index.md` um Codeguardian-Dashboard ergänzen (`→ [[Code-Prüfungen Übersicht]]`) und committen.
4. Finaler Check: `git status --porcelain` → nur beabsichtigte Änderungen übrig.

## Relevant Files
- `.gitignore` — modified, noch nicht committet; enthält neue venv/cache/scratch-Regeln.
- `00-Home/Index.md` — Vault-Hauptindex; frontmatter `updated: 2026-11-11`; Codeguardian-Dashboard-Link fehlt noch.
- `codeguardian/` — ~35 Review-Notes (unversioniert), Dashboard `Code-Prüfungen Übersicht.md`.
- `scripts/verify.py` — cross-platform Verify; Exit 5 bei leerem Target = erwartet.
- `05_Fehler/` — 3 Fehler-Notes (`FEHLER-2026-11-10_verteilstungsplan-health.md`, `FEHLER-2026-11-11_omniroute-413-context-too-large.md`, `FEHLER-2026-11_11_powershell-2147942667-tempdir.md`).

## Important Context
- Branch `freellmapi-isolated`; letzte Commits: `0525c0ec`, `45de29e9`, `ea56029a`.
- Ollama läuft lokal; Reviewer-Modell `ollama/codellama:latest`.
- `git status --porcelain` zeigt nach `ea56029a` noch immer `M .gitignore`, `M OMNI-INBOX.md` sowie ~40 unversionierte Einträge (Vault-Ordner + Scratch-Dateien).
- Der `git add`-Befehl mit `\`-Continuation ist auf PowerShell gescheitert — muss als einzelne Zeile oder Array wiederholt werden.

## Objective
- Vault versionieren: `.gitignore` für Scratch-Dateien finalisieren, `codeguardian/`-Review-Notes und Vault-Verzeichnisse committen. **`code/` darf erst committet werden, wenn Build-Artefakte und Datenbanken per `.gitignore` ausgeschlossen sind.**

## Requirements
- `.env` bleibt ignoriert.
- Conventional Commits auf Deutsch.
- Windows-Kompatibilität (`verify.py` statt `verify.sh`).
- Nur relevante Vault-Bestandteile versionieren; Scratch/Probe-Dateien ignorieren.
- `codeguardian/` explizit tracken.
- **`code/`: Build-Artefakte (`target/`, `*.lib`, `*.rlib`, `*.pdb`), SQLite-Datenbanken, Backups, Venvs, node_modules dürfen nicht in Git.**

## Decisions
- Eingebettetes Git-Repo `02_ECC/` wird mit `M`-Gitlink-Markierung toleriert und nicht committet.
- `codeguardian/` wird versioniert (Review-Notes + Dashboard).
- Legacy-Scratch-Pfade großflächig in `.gitignore` aufgenommen.
- `*.bak` (Zeile 10) erfasst `opencode.json.bak-schemafix-20261107` nicht → eigene Regel `opencode.json.bak-*` (Zeile 11) eingefügt, Wirkung verifiziert.
- **`code/` wird NICHT committet, bis `.gitignore` dort Rust-Target, SQLite, Backups abdeckt.**

## Work State
### Completed
- `.opencode/`-Pipeline committet (`45de29e9`); `auto-review.js` → `verify.py` Fix committet (`0525c0ec`).
- `AGENTS.md`, `AI-System-Core.md`, `EXECUTION_LOOP.md`, `.ecc/test-task/` committet.
- `.gitignore` + `OMNI-INBOX.md` initial committet (`ea56029a`).
- `.gitignore` massiv erweitert; drei Lücken geschlossen: Tippfehler `onenoite-` → `onenote-` (Zeile 105), `temp/` (Zeile 84), `opencode.json.bak-*` (Zeile 11).
- `git check-ignore -v` verifiziert: alle drei Pfade ignoriert.
- `git status --porcelain` zeigt nur erwarteten Bestand (keine Scratch-Dateien mehr).
- `codeguardian/`-Inhalt geprüft: 25 Dateien gesamt, davon 11 untracked.

### Active
- `codeguardian/` committen (11 untracked Artefakte; Dashboard bereits versioniert).
- **`code/.gitignore` erweitern** (Rust `target/`, `*.sqlite`, `db_backups/`, `backups/`, `*.lib`, `*.rlib`, `*.pdb`, `node_modules/`, `.venv/`, `__pycache__/`).
- Vault-Verzeichnisse (`Fehler/`, `INFO-Logs/`, `Projekte/`) + `00-Home/Index.md` + `.gitignore` (Root) committen.
- Finalen `git status --porcelain` als Abschlussdokumentation.

### Blocked
- `code/` kann nicht committet werden, bevor `.gitignore` dort die 13 GB Build-Artefakte/Datenbanken abdeckt.

## Next Move
1. `git add codeguardian/` → Conventional Commit (Deutsch).
2. **`code/.gitignore` erweitern** (siehe Relevant Files) → `git add code/.gitignore` → Commit.
3. `git add .gitignore 00-Home/Index.md Fehler/ INFO-Logs/ Projekte/` → Conventional Commit(s) (Deutsch); `02_ECC`-Gitlink bewusst auslassen.
4. Finalen `git status --porcelain` dokumentieren (erwartet: nur `M 02_ECC` bleibt).

## Relevant Files
- `codeguardian/`: 11 untracked Artefakte (Review-Notes).
- `.gitignore` (Root): modifiziert, uncommitted; Zeilen 10, 11, 84, 105 relevant.
- `code/.gitignore`: **muss erweitert werden** — fehlt: `target/`, `*.sqlite`, `db_backups/`, `backups/`, `*.lib`, `*.rlib`, `*.pdb`, `node_modules/`, `.venv/`, `__pycache__/`, `*.onnx`, `*.dmp`, `*.exe`, `*.dll`, `*.pyd`, `*.bin`, `*.zip`, `*.7z`, `*.tar`, `*.gz`.
- `00-Home/Index.md`: modifiziert (Dashboard-Link), uncommitted.
- `Fehler/`, `INFO-Logs/`, `Projekte/`: untracked Vault-Verzeichnisse, zu versionieren.

## Important Context
- Branch `freellmapi-isolated`; letzter Commit `bdd20823`.
- Offener git status: `M .gitignore`, `M 00-Home/Index.md`, `M 02_ECC` (Gitlink, bewusst uncommittet), `?? Fehler/`, `?? INFO-Logs/`, `?? Projekte/`, `?? code/` (13 GB Junk), `?? codeguardian/*` (11 Dateien).

## Objective
- Code-Subrepo nach `.gitignore`-Versionierung bereinigen: dauerhaft gelöschte `AI-SYSTEM/`-Dateien (Queue-Archiv, Config, Docs) als Commit abschließen.

## Requirements
- Conventional Commits auf Deutsch.
- Windows/pwsh-Umgebung.
- Nur relevante Bestandteile versionieren; Scratch- und Build-Dateien ignorieren.

## Decisions
- Root-Repo: Finalisiert mit Commit `99540387` (Vault-Versionierung).
- Code-Subrepo: `.gitignore` mit Commit `bea8e3f` versioniert.
- Git-Index-Lock entfernt.
- **User-Entscheidung**: Die gelöschten `AI-SYSTEM/`-Dateien dauerhaft committen (nicht wiederherstellen).
- Commit `c4221aa` ausgeführt: `refactor(AI-SYSTEM): altes System entfernen (Config, Queue-Archiv, Docs)` — 123 files changed, 97 insertions(+), 11832 deletions(-).

## Work State
### Completed
- Root-Repo: `.gitignore` aktualisiert, `codeguardian/` tracked, `Projekte/` & `02_ECC/` ignoriert, verwaister Gitlink entfernt.
- Code-Subrepo: `.gitignore` committet (`bea8e3f`).
- Git-Lock beseitigt.
- Löschungen per `git add -u "AI-SYSTEM/"` gestaged.
- Commit `c4221aa` erfolgreich durch Code-Guardian-Hook (Gates + Secret-Regex) gelaufen.
- `AI-SYSTEM/` enthält physikalisch nur noch `src/orchestrator.js` (~4,3 KB, tracked).

### Active
- Endstatus-Verifikation: `git status --short` im Code-Subrepo nach dem Commit noch nicht ausgeführt.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. `git -C "E:\AI-System 3.0\code" status --short` — sauberen Working Tree bestätigen.
2. Vault/OMNI-INBOX-Eintrag für die Bereinigung abschließen (erledigt markieren, Commit-Hash `c4221aa` notieren).

## Relevant Files
- `E:\AI-System 3.0\code\.gitignore`: Versionierte Rust/SQLite/OOM-Regeln (`bea8e3f`).
- `E:\AI-System 3.0\code\AI-SYSTEM\src\orchestrator.js`: Einzige physisch verbliebene Datei; bei `git add -u` LF→CRLF-Warning aufgetreten (vermutlich Ursache der 97 insertions im Commit).
- `E:\AI-System 3.0\.gitignore`: Root-Ignorierdatei (finalisiert).

## Important Context
- Zwei Git-Repositories: Root (`E:\AI-System 3.0`) UND Subrepo (`E:\AI-System 3.0\code`).
- `code/` ist separates Git-Repo; 13 GB Build-Artefakte + 4 eingebettete Standalone-Repos bewusst untracked.
- HEAD `code/`: `bea8e3f` (chore gitignore) → **`c4221aa`** (AI-SYSTEM-Löschungen, aktuell).
- AI-SYSTEM-Historie: Baseline `24ffaa4` → Phase A `f49d1ef` → Phase B+C `a852b30` → Aider runnerEngine `a3ebc60` → Phase D `2d929aa`.
- Abweichung: Erwartet wurden 127 Löschungen; Commit enthält 123 geänderte Dateien (122 deletions + `orchestrator.js`-Modifikation durch CRLF-Normalisierung) — bei Status-Check darauf achten, dass `orchestrator.js` nicht erneut als modified auftaucht.
- Commits laufen durch Code-Guardian-Hook (Gates + Secret-Regex); `c4221aa` hat diese Bestanden.

## Objective
- Code-Subrepo nach `.gitignore`-Versionierung bereinigen: dauerhaft gelöschte `AI-SYSTEM/`-Dateien als Commit abschließen und sauberen Working Tree bestätigen.

## Requirements
- Conventional Commits auf Deutsch.
- Windows/pwsh-Umgebung.
- Nur relevante Bestandteile versionieren; Scratch- und Build-Dateien ignorieren.

## Decisions
- Root-Repo: Finalisiert mit Commit `99540387` (Vault-Versionierung).
- Code-Subrepo: `.gitignore` mit Commit `bea8e3f` versioniert.
- Git-Index-Lock entfernt.
- Gelöschte `AI-SYSTEM/`-Dateien dauerhaft committen (nicht wiederherstellen).
- Commit `c4221aa` ausgeführt: `refactor(AI-SYSTEM): altes System entfernen (Config, Queue-Archiv, Docs)` — 123 files changed, 97 insertions(+), 11832 deletions(-).

## Work State
### Completed
- Root-Repo: `.gitignore` aktualisiert, `codeguardian/` tracked, `Projekte/` & `02_ECC/` ignoriert, verwaister Gitlink entfernt.
- Code-Subrepo: `.gitignore` committet (`bea8e3f`).
- Git-Lock beseitigt.
- Löschungen per `git add -u "AI-SYSTEM/"` gestaged.
- Commit `c4221aa` erfolgreich durch Code-Guardian-Hook (Gates + Secret-Regex) gelaufen.
- `AI-SYSTEM/` enthält physikalisch nur noch `src/orchestrator.js` (~4,3 KB, tracked).

### Active
- Endstatus-Verifikation: `git status --short` im Code-Subrepo zeigt viele unverwahrte Modifikationen — Working Tree ist nicht sauber. Zu prüfen, ob diese Modified-Dateien ignoriert werden sollen oder ob sie vom `.gitignore` abgedeckt werden müssen.

### Blocked
- (none)

1. Klassifizieren der viele `M`-Dateien im Code-Subrepo: sollen sie ignoriert, committet oder gelöscht werden?
2. `agency-agents-app` und `researc[h]` Submodule (`m`-Status) prüfen — sind die Submodule sauber oder haben sie lokale Änderungen?

- `E:\AI-System 3.0\code\docs\`: Workflow-Dateien modifiziert.
- `E:\AI-System 3.0\code\agency-agents-app`: Submodule mit lokalen Änderungen (`m`).

## Important Context
- Zwei Git-Repositories: Root (`E:\AI-System 3.0`) UND Subrepo (`E:\AI-System 3.0\code`).
- `code/` ist separates Git-Repo; 13 GB Build-Artefakte + 4 eingebettete Standalone-Repos bewusst untracked.

## Objective
- Code-Subrepo nach `.gitignore`-Versionierung bereinigen: AI-SYSTEM-Löschungen committen und Working Tree sauber machen.

## Requirements
- Conventional Commits auf Deutsch.
- Windows/pwsh-Umgebung.
- Nur relevante Bestandteile versionieren; Scratch- und Build-Artefakte ignorieren.

## Decisions
- Root-Repo: Finalisiert mit Commit `99540387` (Vault-Versionierung).
- Code-Subrepo: `.gitignore` mit Commit `bea8e3f` versioniert.
- Git-Index-Lock entfernt.
- AI-SYSTEM-Löschungen per Commit `c4221aa` abgeschlossen: `refactor(AI-SYSTEM): altes System entfernen (Config, Queue-Archiv, Docs)` — 123 files changed, 97 insertions(+), 11832 deletions(-).
- Commit `c4221aa` durch Code-Guardian-Hook (Gates + Secret-Regex) gelaufen.

## Work State
### Completed
- Root-Repo `.gitignore` aktualisiert, `codeguardian/` tracked, `Projekte/` & `02_ECC/` ignoriert.
- Code-Subrepo `.gitignore` committet (`bea8e3f`).
- AI-SYSTEM-Löschungen committet (`c4221aa`).
- `AI-SYSTEM/` enthält physikalisch nur noch `src/orchestrator.js` (~4,3 KB, tracked).

### Active
- Working Tree ist nicht sauber: `git status --short` zeigt ~30 Modified-Dateien (`.opencode/opencode.json`, `OMNI-INBOX.md`, `omni-dashboard/*`, `docs/*`, `open-chats.ps1`, etc.).
- Submodule `agency-agents-app` und `researc[h]` haben `m`-Status (lokale Änderungen im Submodule).
- `.gitignore` möglicherweise unvollständig für Dashboard-Logs, Session-Dateien, Build-Artefakte.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Modified-Dateien klassifizieren: welche sollen committet, welche ignoriert werden?
2. `.gitignore` im Code-Subrepo erweitern für nicht-versionierbare Dateien (Logs, Session-State, Tunnel-Files).
3. Submodule-Änderungen prüfen (`agency-agents-app`, `researc[h]`) — Commit oder Ignore?
4. Working Tree bereinigen und sauberen Status bestätigen.
